doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Years in Alaska and construction work
summary: After a break, asked why he moved from construction to music, Gates describes years of construction work around Alaska and the Northwest.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: We’re back. Okay. Okay so I’ll just pick up. What inspired you to move from the construction business into the music world?

Well when I went up there I was going to stay for a year and a year started to go by and I liked living up there. I left one year and went to work in Washington State in construction. I got to sit in a little bit in a couple of places in Olympia and Seattle. I went back to Alaska. I went to Arizona for a season and worked on a road job. Went back to Alaska. Came back to the East Coast for about eight or nine months, went back to Alaska. There was something about it. I mean there’s two things that’ll happen to you if you moved then anyway, because it’s very different now up there. Either you love it and you can’t leave or you want to get out of there as soon as possible. But after being up there for almost twelve years, someone said to me, “You know there’s a summer arts festival up here.” I’d been living, going on for probably eight or nine years. I didn’t know about it because in the summer I was somewhere remote working, which is that’s what I wanted. I didn’t want to be in town. I liked Fairbanks but I liked the out more. I wanted to be out there, I wanted to be in the Brooks Range. I wanted to be on the Arctic Slope. I wanted to be on the Kenai Peninsula. I wanted to be on the Aleutians. I wanted to see what it was all about. And there was this summer arts festival. And I happened to be just coming off of a job. So I’m going to be in town for a month.
